newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-OFFSIDE RULE TO DISAPPEAR.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-OFFSIDE RULE TO DISAPPEAR.

text.p: A rule change aimed at making ice hockey more open and increase scoring was announced by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) on Tuesday.
The centre ice offside rule will be scrapped after next year's Nagano Winter Olympics.

"We will discuss this rule change with the NHL and perhaps they will follow us, I hope so," said IIHF rules committee head Philippe Lacarriere. "We're trying to make the game more offensive, more attractive.
"It's difficult to say how many more goals this will create but when you play without the centre ice red line off-side there is more opportunity."
The rule will apply to all international competitions but it will be up to individual federations to implement the change at a national level.
By removing the centre ice line, which the player cannot cross before receiving a pass from his own end or be ruled off-side, the IIHF has created more space in the neutral zone.
But not everyone, is convinced the change will be positive.
Canadian officials fear the rule change will leave them at a disadvantage internationally since they have no immediate plans to implement the rule in any of their national leagues.
"All the studies we've done are inconclusive," said Bob Nicholson, vice-president of Hockey Canada. "We're concerned about this going internationally especially since it hasn't been tested a lot."
